Byrd and Cummins leaned on their three-shot handicap edge exactly the way alternate shot demands, jumping Harris and Wynn early and never really letting them breathe in a 3&2 Red win. Mercer and Rea never let the Modified Alternate Shot match breathe, converting a hefty 12-stroke handicap edge into a clinical 3&2 win. Ross Montague and Louis Amagliani leaned hard into their seven-shot advantage and never let Red settle, closing out Mac Plosser and Jay Edwards 3&2 in a match that was decided on net efficiency, not highlight reels. John Irvine (playing off scratch in the match) absorbed Brandon Byrd’s four-stroke cushion early, then ran him down and pulled away for a clinical 4&2 win. Ryan Quinn leaned hard into his five-shot net cushion and never let William Harris breathe, rolling to a ruthless 7&5 win that was basically decided before the turn. Hunter Meriwether (18) leaned into his three-shot edge over Allen Bobango (15) and turned the match into a steady net-pressure grind, closing Blue out 3&2. Mac Plosser delivered a clean, front-foot singles performance to take down Luke Jensen 4&3, and he did it by refusing to let Jensen’s nine-stroke net cushion ever become a weapon. Louis Amagliani’s 7-shot handicap edge (24 to Owen Mercer’s 17) decided a match that swung wildly on just a handful of stroke-index holes, with Blue ultimately stealing it 1 up. Daniel Wynn (Blue) stole a 1 UP win from Jay Edwards (Red) in a match that looked gone more than once, especially given Wynn was giving up five strokes in the handicap setup. Drew Hursey (playing off scratch in the match) handled Kevin Rea despite conceding a massive 12-shot net cushion, closing the Singles match 4&3 by simply winning too many holes outright. Ross Montague and Luke Jensen took a 2-up scramble win for Blue, but it didn’t look inevitable early with Red holding a one-stroke handicap edge and actually cashing it immediately. Plosser and Quinn never let the 2-man scramble turn into a handicap hunt, overcoming Blue’s three-shot edge by simply posting the only real separation of the day. Blue never let this 2-man scramble breathe, turning a modest three-stroke match-stroke edge into a runaway 5&4 win by relentlessly cashing the right holes. Mac Plosser and Kyle Cummins turned what started as a punch-for-punch shamble into a runaway, rolling Buck Towner and Drew Hursey 7&5 despite Blue getting the bulk of the handicap help. Win probability mirrored the collapse—Red jumped from roughly even through 6 to 73% by 9, 86% by 10, and a near lock (99%+) by 12. Blue never let this Best Ball match breathe, riding a fast start into a clinical 4&2. Meriwether’s net birdie on 12 restored separation, and Blue kept cashing in net birdies on the par-5s (15) before closing the door with back-to-back outright wins on 16 and 17.

This best-ball finished dead even, but it didn’t feel that way for long stretches because both sides rode their handicap edges at different times. Red’s 2&1 best-ball win was a textbook case of higher-handicap players actually cashing their strokes instead of just carrying them around. Even after Blue squared it at 14, Red’s back-to-back wins at 15 and 16—again led by Bobango’s net 4 and steady net 5—were the closing blows, sending win probability to 91% and leaving the final two holes as formalities.

John Irvine took a 4&3 singles win for Blue by simply refusing to give Ryan Quinn’s three-stroke cushion any room to matter. Quinn briefly made it interesting by winning 9 and 11 to trim it to 1, but Irvine answered immediately at 12, then closed the door with a ruthless three-hole run at 14–16 to stretch it to 5 up and end it early.

Brandon Byrd never let Louis Amagliani’s hefty 14-shot cushion breathe, rolling to a ruthless 6&5 win that was decided by who actually converted those strokes. Kevin Rea’s 18-shot net cushion over Buck Towner should have made this routine, and for long stretches it did—at least on the scoreboard. Edwards kept pressing with wins on 15 and 16 to get 1 up, but Meriwether’s closing 4 on 18 forced the half, and Edwards’ lone late chance to cash in—winning 17 outright—was neutralized net by Meriwether’s two-stroke edge.

Jay Snyder edged Ross Montague 1 up in a net-match-play grinder that swung repeatedly on whether Montague could actually cash the eight strokes he was getting. Mac Plosser outlasted Daniel Wynn 1 UP in a singles match that never let either side breathe, largely because Wynn’s 15-shot cushion created constant pressure on Plosser to win holes outright. Brandon Byrd made his four-shot net edge over Luke Jensen matter immediately and never let the match drift back to even footing, closing out a 3&2 win in this nine-hole set.
